key_insight: WorkflowArena focuses on how well LLMs organize multiple agents into executable workflows—not just whether the system completes a task. It treats workflow orchestration as a distinct capability to evaluate.
problem_solved: As LLMs take responsibility for creating worker agents and coordinating their execution, task-completion scores alone may not reveal the quality of the workflows they design.
method: Benchmark executable workflow orchestration in LLM-based multi-agent systems.
Focus on settings where models instantiate worker agents and author coordination workflows at runtime.
Examine organizational capability beyond end-to-end task completion; detailed evaluation procedures are not available in the provided abstract excerpt.
impact: This evaluation focus could help practitioners assess how effectively LLMs coordinate agent teams, rather than relying only on final task outcomes. The provided excerpt does not include experimental results.
visual_elements: Workflow graph showing an orchestrator creating and connecting worker agents.
Side-by-side diagram contrasting developer-defined and model-authored workflows.
Two-axis evaluation graphic separating task completion from orchestration quality.
Execution timeline illustrating coordination among multiple agents.
paper_title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
paper_authors: Zheng Jiang, Fang Niu, Bo Peng, Houde Qian, Wenyi Li
